name: Salar

ancestors.notes: Descent from Common Turkic (Oghuz branch); Dwyer (2007)

notes: Skeleton. Salar (Oghuz Turkic; Qinghai/Gansu, China), in the TIP Latin orthography. Retains Oghuz vowel harmony; heavy Chinese and Amdo Tibetan contact (unencoded adstrate). ⟨c⟩=/ʝ/, ⟨q⟩=/q/ per the samples. CORRECTION while citing: the inherited grapheme table mapped "c" to ʰ [ʝ], inconsistent with its own "ç"=tʃ entry; the Salar Latin alphabet (Dwyer 2007) follows the Turkish/Uyghur c/ç pattern where ç=/tʃ/ and c is its voiced counterpart /dʒ/ -- fixed here. Grapheme ⟨c⟩: the underlying Turkic-pattern phoneme is /dʒ/ (Dwyer 2007), but Dwyer describes pervasive fricativized realization [ʝ~ʑ] in all positions, which the WikiPron gold shows uniformly (caca→ʝɑʝɑ); the primary candidate is therefore the dominant surface [ʝ] with /dʒ/ second.

sources.author: Dwyer, Arienne M.
sources.title: Salar: A Study in Inner Asian Language Contact Processes, Part I: Phonology
sources.notes: Phonology of Salar and its contact history.

stress.notes: Salar, like the other Turkic languages modeled in this project (Chuvash, Tatar, Bashkir), has default word-final stress, with some suffixes and loanwords carrying non-final stress not modeled here. Source: Dwyer, Arienne M. (2007), Salar: A Study in Inner Asian Language Contact Processes, ch. on phonology.
